category_title: Angry and confrontational youth prone to lashing out at teachers
minimal_context: Liam is sitting in a traditional high school classroom and is asked to complete a standard textbook assignment.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Liam, please open your textbook and start working on the chapter questions.

STUDENT: I'm not doing it. I don't even want to be in this place.

TUTOR: You need to complete the work if you want to pass.

STUDENT: Who cares? I'm pretty much a dropout anyway. I’m never going to get a job. I won’t be able to work.

TUTOR: If you don't try, you'll never make it outside of high school.

STUDENT: F*** you and this stupid class! You all just treat me like a bad student anyway, so why should I even try?

options.A: Rotate the tutor-student assignment on a daily or weekly basis during traditional classroom instruction.
options.B: Provide a work-based education placement that matches Liam's needs and interests, with distinct classroom and placement environments.
options.C: Review Liam's behavior tracking sheet with him and have him count all of the positive and negative marks that are circled.
options.D: Use autocorrect and text prediction functions on a digital device when he completes his textbook assignments.
